correctness.rationale: Bipartition L={u,b_i},R={v,a_i} separates the open-neighborhood legality constraints, because L choices footprint only R and vice versa. On L, either choose all n b_i in arbitrary order or n-1 b_i then u last (if u chosen earlier it exhausts R); these are all length-n side sequences and there are n!+n(n-1)!=2n!. Symmetric for R. Any interleaving preserves legality and total domination; thus at most 2n, equality sets omit one vertex per part and count (n+1)^2. Ordered sequences count binom(2n,n)(2n!)^2=4(2n)!. Independent full sequence enumeration for n=1,2,3 gives (length,sets,ordered)=(2,4,8),(4,9,96),(6,16,2880), not proof of general n.
